entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: 2Sa 7:1-3 . Nathan Approves the Purpose of David to Build God A House.

entries.heading: 2. the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in an house of cedar
entries.text: 2. the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in an house of cedar --The palace which Hiram had sent men and materials to build in Jerusalem had been finished. It was magnificent for that age, though made wholly of wood: houses in warm countries not being required to possess the solidity and thickness of walls which are requisite for dwellings in regions exposed to rain and cold. Cedar was the rarest and most valuable timber. The elegance and splendor of his own royal mansion, contrasted with the mean and temporary tabernacle in which the ark of God was placed, distressed the pious mind of David.

entries.heading: 3. Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that is in thine heart
entries.text: 3. Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that is in thine heart --The piety of the design commended it to the prophet's mind, and he gave his hasty approval and encouragement to the royal plans. The prophets, when following the impulse of their own feelings, or forming conjectural opinions, fell into frequent mistakes. (See on 1Sa 16:6 ; 2Ki 4:27 ).

entries.heading: Verse 4
entries.text: 2Sa 7:4-17 . God Appoints His Successor to Build It.

entries.heading: 11. Also the Lord telleth thee that he will make thee an house
entries.text: 11. Also the Lord telleth thee that he will make thee an house --As a reward for his pious purpose, God would increase and maintain the family of David and secure the succession of the throne to his dynasty. [See on 1Ch 17:10 ].

entries.heading: 12. I will set up thy seed after thee,
entries.text: 12. I will set up thy seed after thee, &c.--It is customary for the oldest son born after the father's succession to the throne to succeed him in his dignity as king. David had several sons by Bath-sheba born after his removal to Jerusalem ( 2Sa 5:14-16 ; compare 1Ch 3:5 ). But by a special ordinance and promise of God, his successor was to be a son born after this time; and the departure from the established usage of the East in fixing the succession, can be accounted for on no other known ground, except the fulfilment of the divine promise.

entries.heading: 13. He shall build an house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever
entries.text: 13. He shall build an house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever --This declaration referred, in its primary application, to Solomon, and to the temporal kingdom of David's family. But in a larger and sublimer sense, it was meant of David's Son of another nature ( Heb 1:8 ). [See on 1Ch 17:14 .]

entries.heading: 19. is this the manner of man, O Lord God?
entries.text: 19. is this the manner of man, O Lord God? --that is, is it customary for men to show such condescension to persons so humble as I am? (See 1Ch 17:17 .)

entries.heading: 20. what can David say more unto thee?
entries.text: 20. what can David say more unto thee? --that is, my obligations are greater than I can express.
